learning_outcomes.text: Understand and evaluate the process of generation, transport, distribution, and storage of electrical energy, with special emphasis on generation and storage processes for remote applications.
Analyze and size the protection systems of a simple low-voltage installation.

Understand the specific characteristics that distinguish power diodes and MOSFET transistors from signal ones, and understand the operation of other electronic devices used exclusively in power applications (IGBTs, SCRs, Triacs, and GTOs).
Understand the operation of uncontrolled single-phase and three-phase rectifiers and calculate voltages and currents in their components.
Analyze, quantify, and design linear power supplies.
Understand the operation of basic DC/DC converters and single-phase DC/AC converters and calculate voltages and currents in their components.
Analyze the operation of simple power electronic systems of special interest in the world of telecommunications.
Perform simulation of general-purpose electronic circuits with computer tools.
Select semiconductor devices and power capacitors for a known application.
Calculate power magnetic components (coils and transformers) for a known application.
Understand the operation of controlled and semi-controlled single-phase and three-phase rectifiers and calculate voltages and currents in their components.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. The electric power distribution network
Topic 2. Other sources of electrical energy
Topic 6. Principles of switched DC-DC conversion: Pulse width modulators
Topic 8. Electronic devices for power electronic converters
Topic 9. Examples of power electronic systems for telecommunications
assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, the final grade is calculated as 20% Laboratory Practices (PL) + 80% Theory, provided that a minimum of 3 out of 10 points is achieved in each evaluable component. The theory grade is composed of 18% B1, 12% B2, 20% B3.A, and 50% B3.B. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of 4 and the weighted sum. For extraordinary examination, the PL grade from the ordinary exam is retained, and the theoretical part is re-evaluated for blocks where the minimum was not met, calculating Theory as 18% B1 + 12% B2 + 70% B3. For differentiated evaluation, a practical exam and a theoretical exam divided into B1, B2, B3 with minimums of 3 points per block are assessed with 20% and 80% weights respectively.
